packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response; packets 02 and 14 completed by further fresh readers after a display cap hid images, packet 17 reread by a fresh reader
text:
PACKET-14: UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind first reader)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE NOTES
- Nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading of this text. I did not open packet.json, any edition, catalogue, or earlier transcription.
- One identifier is written on the object itself: a modern pencil note on the right edge of the leaf (image-026, also image-022) reads approximately "Stams, StA, Frg. 31v". I note it as an observation only. I did not use it to identify anything.
- Beyond the rules: to read text that runs sideways or upside down, I made rotated and cropped/enlarged copies of tiles 002, 003, 004, 010, 014, 023, 028, 029, 032 and 033 in a session scratch directory outside the packet. I read only those derived copies and the packet images.
- Coverage limit: when I first tried to open tiles 005, 009, 012, 013, 015, 016, 017 and overview 018, the tool returned "media removed: request limit". I never viewed these images directly. I saw the areas of 002, 003, 004 and 014 through my rotated copies. I viewed overview 001 and tiles 006, 007, 008, 010, 011 and 019-034. The right-column bottom (009/013), the lower margin (015-017) and overview 018 are therefore unread by me.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Overview 001 and tiles 019-034 show one side of a binding leaf in two states. In 001 a strip of an older book-hand manuscript is folded over the top edge as a turn-in. In the 019-034 set the turn-ins are positioned differently (tiles 019-022 show the book-hand strip at the top, upside down; tiles 027-033 show more book-hand text, upside down, at the bottom). I treat it as one face photographed twice and do not count overlapping lines twice.
- MAIN LAYER: a later, small, current cursive hand. There is a ruled frame and two columns: col. a on the left (tiles 006/007/010/011, = 023/024) and col. b on the right (tiles 007/008/011, = 024/025). A grey-blue stain covers much of the surface.
  * The text alternates two grades. Short lines in larger cursive (e.g. "Em dat et en ...", "Est primo varia ...", "Dicas ...", "Est sub stans nec ... nabile nomen") carry small interlinear glosses ("ss(cilicet) ..."). Longer blocks in smaller cursive follow them.
  * Tentative interpretation: the larger lines are quoted lemmata (verse-like) and the smaller blocks are commentary. Col. b is commentary-style prose throughout.
  * Faint large-letter headings at the top of both columns (above the ruled frame) are illegible.
- LOWER BAND (tiles 028-030): more lemma lines in larger cursive with interlinear glosses, written over a heavy green/brown stain.
- LEFT-EDGE STRIP (tiles 010/014, and 023): a narrow strip of the same or a similar cursive with lines running vertically. It is a separate pasted strip or turn-in. The strip in the 001 state (014) and the one in the 019-034 state (023) carry different text.
- OLDER BOOK-HAND STRIP (turn-in; tiles 002-004 rotated, 019-022, 027-033): textualis in one column. It has alternating red and blue flourished initials (Q, S, Q, E, h) and red rubrics, partly abraded.
- MIRROR OFFSET: tile 028 (lower right, the column under the lower band) shows a block of textualis that reads in mirror image. It is probably an offset or transfer from a facing leaf, not text written on this face. I did not transcribe it.

SELECTED SPANS
A. Col. a, lemma lines and commentary (image-006, continued in image-007; same lines in 023/024)
B. Col. a, second lemma group and commentary (image-010/011)
C. Col. b commentary (image-008)
D. Lower band lemma lines (image-028/029/030)
E. Left-edge cursive strip (image-014, rotated)
F. Left-edge cursive strip, second state (image-023, rotated)
G. Book-hand turn-in (image-002/003/004, rotated)
Line numbers count from the top of the named image. For rotated strips they count in reading order in my rotated copy.
Conventions: ( ) expansion; ? after an uncertain word; [illegible] unread. The cursive is heavily abbreviated, and many expansions are guesses.

=== A. Col. a (image-006; the right-hand ends of the lines are in image-007) ===

----------------------------------------------------------------
image-001 (overview, reduced): a parchment leaf reused as a binding/wrapper,
with a folded-over flap at the top (text there runs sideways, written by a
different, smaller, more formal hand with red and blue initials), a narrow
turned-in strip at the left (text running vertically), and a turn-in strip at
the bottom (one line of text, inverted relative to the main face). The main
face shows two columns of a cursive, heavily abbreviated hand (late-medieval
cursiva/bastarda-like; no date inferred). Ruled frame visible in both columns.
Left column: short one-line headings set off from the prose, e.g. a line
beginning "Est sub stans(?) ..." and "Duo quero(?) ...", followed by blocks of
prose; spacing suggests headings/lemmata followed by commentary (tentative).
Right column: continuous prose, many lines, no headings visible at this scale.
Binding-thread stitch stations cross both columns about two-thirds down; a hole
in the left column. Lower part of both columns blank below the text block.

image-018 (second overview, reduced): the same object photographed with the
flaps folded differently, exposing more of the other text-bearing material:
a two-column formal gothic text with red/blue initials across the lower half,
a large green-stained band across the middle, and a red/blue "VII" at the lower
left edge. Lines visible at overview scale in a larger formal script in the
green band: "... P(ue)r natus est nobis filius da[tus] ..." and below it
"... cui(us) i(m)p(er)iu(m) sup(er) humeru(m) ..."; further right "...glie(?) in
manu d(omi)ni ..." (reading at overview scale only, uncertain). These appear to
be a different text and hand from the cursive grammatical columns; I did not
have native-resolution tiles of that area in my set.

a red ruling trace. Lower right: pencil label partly visible "...frg. 31v".
